docs.text: Getting Started Installation If you have a GPU and have the drivers installed and up-to-date, the install should be as simple as cloning the repository and using pip. We recommend installing in editable mode with git clone https://github.com/cronos-inria/tractography.git cd tractography pip install -e . If you would like to use the CPU version, then we recommend using anaconda for the installation conda create -n tractography python=3 conda activate tractography conda install anaconda::binutils conda install numpy conda install -c conda-forge pocl conda install -c conda-forge pyopencl git clone https://github.com/cronos-inria/tractography.git cd tractography pip install -e . Quickstart (Python) The example below runs a complete tractography workflow in Python using synthetic test data generated by test.data.cross() . It uses the transport algorithm and saves a tractogram to disk. from pathlib import Path import nibabel as nib import tractography as tg import tg.data # Load the crossing fibres dataset using spherical harmonics. You can replace # this by your own FOD data. fod, wm, _ = tg.data.sh.cross() # Generate seeds from the white-matter mask and track only in the white matter. n_seeds = 100 # In practice, many more seeds would be used. seeds = tg.seeds.from_mask(wm.get_fdata(), wm.affine, n_seeds) fod = tg.nifti.multiply(fod, wm) # This masks the FOD outside of the WM. # Load and tweak the transport configuration. config = tg.configuration.load(tg.Algorithm.TRANSPORT) config.batch_size = n_seeds # Run tractography. tractogram = tg.tractogram(fod, seeds, config) # Save outputs. output_dir = Path("quickstart-output") output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) nib.save(fod, output_dir / "cross_fod.nii.gz") nib.save(wm, output_dir / "cross_wm.nii.gz") nib.streamlines.save(tractogram, output_dir / "cross_transport_streamlines.tck") You can then visualize the results in your favorite viewer. The result should look something like this.
